chunks: Hadith 3780 — It is narrated from Khālid ibn Ḥajjāj al-Karkhī, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “I buy food on deferred terms until a specified time, then the merchants seek it from me after I have bought it, before I take possession of it.” He said:

“There is no harm in selling on deferred terms as you bought it, but you do not have the right to hand it over or take possession.” I said: “Then when I have taken possession of it, may I be your ransom, do I have the right to hand it over by its measure?” He said: “There is no harm in that if they are satisfied.”

And he عليه السلام said: “Any food that you purchase from a threshing floor or a district, and then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brings destruction upon it, then the buyer is entitled only to his principal. And whatever he buys of described food, without specifying in it a village or a place, then it is upon its owner to deliver it.”

He said: And I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “I buy food from a man, then sell it to another man before I measure it out, and I say: ‘Send your agent so that he may witness its measuring when I take possession of it.’” He said: “There is no harm.”

key_terms.إِلَى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى: on deferred terms until a specified time
key_terms.بَيْدَرٍ: a threshing floor or grain collection place
key_terms.طَعَامًا: food as the commodity under discussion in sale transactions

ai.seo_question: Can food be sold before taking possession of it in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses rulings concerning the sale of food before possession, deferred transactions, and delivery by measure. It clarifies when resale is permitted, limits what may be done before possession, and distinguishes between goods tied to a specific place and goods sold by description.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3780 - It is narrated from Khalid ibn Hajjaj Al-Karkhi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (as): "I buy food on deferred payment until a specified time, and then merchants request to buy it from me before I take possession of it."
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in selling it on deferred payment, as you purchased it, but you are not allowed to hand it over or take possession of it before you actually receive it."
I asked: "Once I take possession of it, may I be your ransom, can I then hand it over using its measured amount?"
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in that if they are satisfied with it."
Imam (as) also said: "Any food you purchase from a field (baydar) or a district (tassuj), and then Allah (swt) causes it to perish, the buyer is only entitled to his principal amount.
But if he purchases food with a general description and does not specify a village or location, then the seller is obligated to deliver it."
I further asked Abu Abdillah (as): "I buy food from a man and then sell it to another man before measuring it, saying to him, 'Send your agent to witness its measurement when I take possession of it.'"
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in that."
